extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for Open Access Pub (academic reviewers; especially those new to reviewing)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for evaluating submitted journal manuscripts, covering section-by-section quality standards, formatting, ethical obligations, and reviewer conduct for Open Access Pub.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title clarity and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Should be readily understood, clear and concise, informative, and directly related to the content of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title must communicate the subject and be directly tied to manuscript content; avoid vague or misleading phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: hypothesis or purpose clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypothesis or purpose should be clear and concise, typically stated in the last sentence of the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the primary aim or hypothesis is explicit and located early (often final sentence of first paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: methodology summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology clearly identified and described briefly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should succinctly state study design and main methods used so readers understand approach at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: results summarised
rubrics_metrics.description: Results summarised with data and statistics where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include key quantitative findings and relevant statistics in the abstract when they are essential to the conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: conclusions stated
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions and findings clearly stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should end with a clear statement of the study's main conclusions or implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: early problem introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Early introduction of the general problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The introduction should open by situating the research within a broader problem area before narrowing to specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: research questions precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Precisely stated research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check that research questions are explicit and unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: hypothesis clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear and concise hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesis should be stated plainly and tied to the research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: study assumptions identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of study assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should declare key assumptions that underpin the design or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: significance discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance of the problem discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The introduction should explain why the problem matters and its relevance to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: justification of research
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must justify why the study is needed (gap in knowledge, practical need, theoretical contribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: literature summary and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief summary of relevant literature and its implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise review showing how prior work leads to the current study and how results will add to the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: citation relevance and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance and timeliness of citations; primary sources preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer recent primary sources (journal articles) over secondary sources (textbooks); ensure citations are current and pertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: relationship to previous research
rubrics_metrics.description: Relationship to previous research clearly established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explicitly connect the study to earlier findings and indicate novelty or replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: subject population description
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject population clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include demographic, inclusion/exclusion criteria, recruitment methods and sample size details necessary to understand the population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: human subjects ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: For human subjects: informed consent or IRB approval documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts with human participants must report ethical approval and consent procedures; absence should be flagged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: animal subjects compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: For animal subjects: compliance with NIH “Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals” (Publication 85-23, revised 1985).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal studies must document compliance with accepted animal welfare guidelines and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: sampling method justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling method justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explain and defend their sampling approach (random, convenience, stratified, etc.) relative to study goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: data collection detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collection methods described with sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough procedural detail for readers to understand how data were obtained; reviewers should ask for more detail if unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: appropriate design
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate design for the hypothesis or research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study design must align with the research question (e.g., randomized trial for causal claims, observational designs for associations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: proper controls included
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper controls included where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for presence and adequacy of control groups/conditions necessary to isolate effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: variables unambiguously identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables unambiguously identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define independent, dependent, and covariates clearly, including measurement instruments and units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: replicability of design
rubrics_metrics.description: Design sufficiently detailed for replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide procedural steps, instruments, materials, and settings so other researchers could reproduce the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: appropriate statistical tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical tests appropriate to the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that chosen tests match data types and design assumptions; if unsure, note on the 'Comments by Editor' form for statistical consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: clarity and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear, precise, and logically organised presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results should follow a logical sequence, be concise, and avoid interpretation that belongs in the Discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: sufficient information to answer question
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient information to answer the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure results include necessary metrics, effect sizes, confidence intervals, and any other data needed to support conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: statistical reporting with values
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical reports with values where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report test statistics, degrees of freedom, p-values, effect sizes, and confidence intervals as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: statistics relevant to hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics relevant to the research hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reporting irrelevant statistics; focus analyses that directly address the study hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: complete, understandable tables and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete, easily understandable tables and figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables/figures should be self-contained with clear labels, units, legends, and footnotes explaining abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: avoid dual reporting in tables and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Data should be reported in either table or figure format—not both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If significant descriptive data exist, consider asking authors to include it as a table addendum rather than duplicating content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: conclusions supported by evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly stated conclusions supported by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions must follow logically from results; avoid overstating findings or making unsubstantiated claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: hypothesis revisited
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypothesis revisited in light of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explicitly relate results back to the original hypotheses and research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: implications discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: Implications of findings discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss theoretical, practical, or policy implications and situate findings within the broader field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: appropriate generalisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper generalisation relative to the study population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authors limit generalisations to populations or contexts supported by their sample and design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: sampling bias and error sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible sources of sampling bias or errors described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should acknowledge and discuss potential biases and their likely impact on results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: relevance and reliability of prior data
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance and reliability of previous research data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how previous studies relate and whether earlier data are reliable or comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: limitations identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations of the study identified and discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must transparently state study limitations and how they affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: recommendations for future research
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete suggestions for follow-up studies or ways to address limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion: summary paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: An end paragraph of the discussion section summarising key findings. A summary paragraph may precede the conclusion if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper should finish with a concise paragraph reiterating the main findings and their significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: style and primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: References must be organised in the required style of the journal. Primary sources (journals) are preferred over secondary sources (textbooks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check citation format adherence and favor citations to original research rather than textbooks or reviews where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: sufficient citation coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should contain sufficient references to previously published work to support the discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure literature cited adequately frames the study; flag omissions of key prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: recommended counts by manuscript type
rubrics_metrics.description: General guidelines for reference counts by manuscript type: Clinical Scientific 20–30; Laboratory Scientific 20–30; Case Report 3–10; How-To 3–10; Review 50–150.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these ranges as loose expectations—not strict rules—when assessing adequacy of referencing for manuscript type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables & Figures: clarity and concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and figures should present results clearly and concisely. Good graphical representation is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability, labeling, and whether graphics aid comprehension; prefer clarity over decorative complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables & Figures: advanced formats acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced 2D and 3D formats may enhance readability, but images must not be manipulated to fit results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 3D or advanced visualisations are acceptable if they genuinely aid interpretation; check for inappropriate image manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables & Figures: video inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Video clips of limited size may be included if they substantially support the findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Videos should be directly relevant and add value; file size and format must meet journal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form & Style: logical organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report must be clear and logically organised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess overall flow, section structure, and readability; request re-organisation if sections are jumbled or repetitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form & Style: impartial tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone should be impartial, unbiased, and scientific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag subjective language, promotional tone, or unscientific wording; recommend neutral, evidence-based phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form & Style: follow journal formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript must follow the journal’s Instructions for Authors format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check adherence to required structure, headings, word counts, and submission templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form & Style: appropriate keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Must contain appropriate keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords should reflect main topics and aid discoverability; suggest edits if keywords are missing or irrelevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer practice: error reporting with line numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Note errors or comments with reference to line numbers, presenting both the issue and the suggested correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise, line-referenced comments and actionable suggestions rather than vague criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer practice: impartial review and revision rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not hesitate to provide an impartial review—multiple rounds of revision may be necessary to achieve the desired quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be candid about needed changes and expect iterative revisions; focus on improving manuscript quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer practice: scope mismatch handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts that fall outside the scope of the journal should be flagged for rejection without a full review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending rejection for scope reasons, state the reason clearly and, where appropriate, suggest alternatives (e.g., language editing or different journals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer practice: language quality expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to high standards of language quality. Published work must be understandable by readers worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend language editing when writing quality impedes comprehension; do not reject solely for grammar if the science is sound but suggest remedial steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: unbiased consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Give unbiased consideration to all manuscripts, judging each on its merits without regard to race, religion, nationality, sex, seniority, or institutional affiliation of the author(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scientific quality only; avoid implicit biases and assess content objectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: timeliness and attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider manuscripts with all reasonable speed and attention. The sole responsibility for acceptance or rejection rests with the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return timely reviews and thorough assessments; understand final decision authority lies with editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not disclose information about manuscripts under consideration to anyone other than those from whom professional advice is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strict confidentiality; any consultation should be with the editor's approval and limited to necessary experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: respect authors' intellectual independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect the intellectual independence of authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imposing personal theories or priorities; critique methodology and interpretation, not authors' rights to explore ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: non-use of unpublished material
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use unpublished information or interpretations from submitted manuscripts in your own research without the author’s consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submitted manuscript informs your work, disclose and obtain permission before using unique ideas or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: conflict of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript is closely related to your own research and creates a conflict of interest, notify the editor so another qualified reviewer can be assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recuse yourself or disclose conflicts; notify editor promptly to allow reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: honour author reviewer-exclusion requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Honour reasonable author requests to exclude specific reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors typically consider author exclusions; if you are aware of an exclusion that affects your ability to review, notify the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical concern escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are unsure about the adequacy of statistical test selection, note this on the 'Comments by Editor' form and a statistical consultation will be arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag statistical doubts for editor-arranged expert review rather than attempting to adjudicate complex statistical issues yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Images must not be manipulated to fit results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for inappropriate cropping, contrast adjustment, or duplications; request original image data if manipulation is suspected.
